info.title: GSM Supplier API
info.description:
REST API v1 and the Dhru Fusion compatible endpoint for GSM merchants, plus the webhook events we send.

**Authentication.** REST API v1 takes `Authorization: Bearer <API key>`; a key has scopes, an optional IP allowlist and its own rate limit. The Dhru Fusion endpoint takes the `username` and `apiaccesskey` form fields.

**Conventions.** JSON bodies use camelCase names. Money is a string with exactly four decimals (`"12.4900"`), timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds (`"2026-03-01T09:30:00.000Z"`) and ids are numbers. Errors are `application/problem+json` with a stable `code`; quote the `requestId` when you contact support.

post.description: The Dhru Fusion v6.1 compatible endpoint (decision 026): `username`, `apiaccesskey`, `action` and `parameters` (base64 of a JSON object) as a form body (`multipart/form-data` and JSON are accepted too). Eight actions: `accountinfo`, `imeiservicelist`, `placeimeiorder`, `placeimeiorderbulk`, `getimeiorder`, `getimeiorderbulk`, `placefileorder` and `getfileorder`. Every answer is HTTP 200 with the headers `X-Powered-By: DHRU-FUSION` and `dhru-fusion-api-version: 6.1` and the body `{ "SUCCESS": [ ... ], "apiversion": "6.1" }` or `{ "ERROR": [ { "MESSAGE": "..." } ], "apiversion": "6.1" }`; a bulk action answers `{ "<request id>": { "SUCCESS" | "ERROR": [ ... ] }, ..., "apiversion": "6.1" }`. A wrong credential is "Authentication Failed", an unknown action "Invalid Action". The key must carry the `dhru` scope; the allowed addresses and the per-minute limit of the key apply.

oneOf.description: Account info. The merchant's available balance (`credit`: the wallet balance plus the credit limit), email and currency. The key `AccoutInfo` is spelled as in the Dhru Fusion standard.

oneOf.title: imeiservicelist
oneOf.description: IMEI service list. The IMEI, server and remote services the merchant may order, grouped by category, at its own price (`CREDIT`), with the quantity rules and the custom fields (`Requires.Custom`). File services are not listed. Archived and disabled services and categories the merchant's group may not see are never listed. Every price shown is remembered as the merchant's listed price (user rule 9).

parameters.description: This action takes no parameters.

QNT.description: `1` when the service sells more than one quantity.

QNTOPTIONS.description: The packs a service sells, comma separated; `""` when it sells a range.

oneOf.title: placeimeiorder
oneOf.description: Place an IMEI, server or remote order. Orders a service at the merchant's own price and holds it from the wallet. `ID` is the `SERVICEID` of `imeiservicelist`; an IMEI service takes `IMEI`, a server or remote service its custom fields in `CUSTOMFIELD`. The answer is immediate: `REFERENCEID` is our order id (status 0). A price that rose more than the tolerance above the price last listed is refused with "Price changed. Please refresh the service list and order again."; a balance that is too low with "Not enough credits". A File service is placed with `placefileorder`.

apiaccesskey.description: A merchant API key with the `dhru` scope.

parameters.description: Base64 of a JSON object; its shape is in `x-gsm-decoded`.

QNT.description: The quantity; defaults to the service's minimum.

CUSTOMFIELD.description: The values of the service custom fields by field name: base64 of a JSON object (an object is accepted too).

IMEI.description: The IMEI of an IMEI service (15 digits, Luhn); leave it out for a server or remote service.

oneOf.title: placeimeiorderbulk
oneOf.description: Place several orders. `parameters` is an object keyed by the caller's request id, each entry the parameters of `placeimeiorder`. The answer has one entry per request id: `{ "SUCCESS": [...] }` or `{ "ERROR": [...] }`. Each order is placed on its own (a refused one never stops the others); at most 100 per call.

oneOf.title: placefileorder
oneOf.description: Place a file order. Orders a File service. The file is `FILENAME` and `FILEDATA` (base64) in `parameters`, or a file part of a `multipart/form-data` request; it is stored like `POST /v1/files` (up to 25 MiB). A form body of this endpoint may be up to 25 MiB (every other route keeps 1 MiB); `FILEDATA` is base64 inside the base64 `parameters`, so about 13 MiB of file fits a form: send a larger file as a multipart file part. Everything else is as `placeimeiorder`. A service that is not a File service is refused. If the order is refused (changed price, not enough credits), the uploaded file is not kept.

post.description: Uploads one file (`multipart/form-data` with one part named `file`, any media type, 1 byte to 25 MiB). The name is reduced to its base name without control characters (at most 200 characters). The object goes to the files bucket and a file owned by the merchant is recorded with its size and SHA-256. A missing or empty file is `422` on `file`; more than 25 MiB is `413`. The id is what a File service order takes as its input file (`fileId` of `POST /v1/orders`). Maintenance with the order scope refuses the upload like an order. Scope `orders:write`.

post.description: Orders a service at the merchant's own price (the one price resolver). The price is held from the wallet in the same transaction. An order that would cost more than the tolerance above the price the merchant last listed is refused with `409 PRICE_CHANGED` (`listedPrice` and `currentPrice` in the body: list the services again and order again), a smaller raise is charged and recorded. A second open order for the same service and input is refused under the service's `block_open` rule (`DUPLICATE_ORDER`). An IMEI service takes `imei` (15 digits, Luhn); a server or remote service takes `inputs`; a File service a `fileId` and/or `inputs`. The answer is immediate: the order is `pending` (or already `completed` when the service delivers from stock). Send an `Idempotency-Key` so that a retry never places a second order; the answer is kept 7 days (a retry later than that places a new order). Scope `orders:write`.

parameters.description: Makes a retry safe: the first answer is stored with the key and sent again for the same request; another request with the key is `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`, one still running `409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`. The answer is kept 7 days from the first request; after that the stored answer is gone and the same key places a new order.

post.description: Places up to 100 orders in one request, each item exactly as `POST /v1/orders` would (the price, the price guard, the duplicate rule, the hold). The answer has one result per item, in the order sent: `ok: true` with the order, or `ok: false` with the refusal (`code`, `status`, `detail`, field `errors`, and `listedPrice` and `currentPrice` for a changed price). An item that is refused places nothing and never stops the others; the items draw on one wallet in the order sent, so a later item may be refused for lack of funds. The answer is `200` even when every item was refused. An `Idempotency-Key` stores the whole answer and replays it for 7 days (after that the stored answer is gone and the same key places new orders).
